summary: Analysis of 14 days of telemetry demonstrates exceptional glycemic control with 99.7% Time in Range (70-180 mg/dL), 0.0% Time Below Range (<70 mg/dL), average glucose of 117.0 mg/dL, and low glycemic variability (CV 12.9%). Active AAPS profile settings, basal rates, carb ratios, and safety limits are well-calibrated and operate in harmony with open-loop and closed-loop delivery.

analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry coverage is 100.0% across 14 days with zero gaps exceeding 15 minutes. 32 treatment records and an authoritative AAPS profile provide complete data for analysis.
analysis_steps.evidence: 1,345 CGM entries, 28 carb entries, 28 meal boluses, and valid active profile payload.

analysis_steps.findings: Glycemic outcomes are well within clinical safety targets, with zero time below range and minimal time above range (0.3%). Glucose variability is low (SD 15.1 mg/dL, CV 12.9%).
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 99.7%, TBR 0.0%, TAR 0.3%, Mean 117.0 mg/dL. Minimal nadirs reached 70 mg/dL on two isolated occasions at 03:00 local time.

analysis_steps.findings: Scheduled basal rates effectively maintain fasting and overnight glucose stability without drift. Target ranges (90-115 mg/dL) are appropriate and reliably attained.
analysis_steps.evidence: Overnight local hourly mean glucose stays between 102.3 mg/dL and 107.5 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.findings: Carb ratios and ISF settings are well-calibrated. Postprandial glucose excursions return to baseline within 4 hours. DIA of 5.5 hours matches observed insulin action tails.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekday breakfast and dinner postprandial glucose curves resolve cleanly by 240 minutes. Weekend brunch peaks at 188 mg/dL due to high fat/protein content but returns to 115 mg/dL by 240 minutes.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM settings effectively manage postprandial glucose rises without causing late-phase hypoglycemia or excessive IOB accumulation.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB interval 3 min, max SMB basal minutes 45 min, and max UAM basal minutes 30 min operate cleanly during meal windows with 0% TBR.
data_gaps: Specific SMB activation boolean flags are null in the raw profile payload and require UI verification.

analysis_steps.findings: Max basal (2.4 U/h) and Max IOB (8.0 U) limits provide sufficient headroom for automated corrections while preventing over-delivery.
analysis_steps.evidence: Peak scheduled basal is 1.05 U/h, providing a safe ~2.3x multiplier for Max Basal. Total daily insulin averages ~10.1 U.
data_gaps: Autosens and Dynamic Sensitivity activation switches are null in profile raw settings.

analysis_steps.findings: Current prebolus times (20 min for breakfast, 10 min for brunch) and immediate bolus split percentages align well with carbohydrate absorption speed.
analysis_steps.evidence: 28 recorded meal boluses match declared timing and yield stable 4-hour post-meal recovery.

analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbohydrate modeling (20 g e-carbs over 120 min) for mixed weekend brunches successfully directs UAM/SMB to handle delayed absorption without postprandial spikes or late lows.
analysis_steps.evidence: Weekend brunches return to baseline (+1 to -11 mg/dL change at 240 min) with zero hypoglycemia.

analysis_steps.findings: All parameters are well-optimized. The primary recommendation is to maintain all core profile settings and verify UI-only switch settings in the AAPS application.
analysis_steps.evidence: Consistent 99.7% TIR and low variability across 14 days confirm overall system synergy.

strengths: Exceptional 99.7% Time in Range with 0.0% Time Below Range over a 14-day period.
Overnight fasting glucose stability is excellent, averaging ~104 mg/dL with minimal variation.
Carbohydrate ratios and prebolus timing effectively control postprandial glucose peaks.
AAPS safety settings (Max Basal 2.4 U/h and Max IOB 8 U) protect against insulin stacking while enabling effective SMB responses.

recommendations.title: Verify AAPS Activation Switches in UI
recommendations.description: Some raw configuration boolean flags (such as smb_always_enabled and autosens_enabled) are reported as null in the profile export context. Verify these settings directly within the AAPS mobile interface to ensure they match your intended preferences.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Maintain all current basal rates, carb ratios, ISF values, and target segments. Current configuration achieves optimal clinical outcomes with 99.7% TIR and 0.0% TBR.
profile_recommendation.rationale: 14-day telemetry confirms excellent fasting stability and postprandial recovery. No adjustments to basal, CR, ISF, or DIA are indicated.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Perform a routine fasting basal check overnight (00:00-06:00) if daily routines, activity levels, or meal schedules change significantly.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight glucose remains flat and stable between 102 and 107 mg/dL with no hypoglycemia.
Morning fasting glucose is stable with smooth transition into breakfast hours.
Afternoon baseline glucose is well-maintained with minimal closed-loop drift.
Evening basal holds glucose steady before and after dinner.
Overnight carb ratio segment is stable and supported by profile baseline.
Weekday breakfast boluses return smoothly to baseline within 3 to 4 hours.
Weekend brunch meal boluses resolve completely without post-meal hypoglycemia.
Dinner meal boluses result in minimal peak rises (+15 to +41 mg/dL) and clean recovery.
Overnight corrections, when required, act predictably without over-hypo risk.
Morning sensitivity setting provides appropriate SMB and correction responsiveness.
Midday ISF maintains safe automated closed-loop adjustments.
Evening ISF handles post-dinner glucose control smoothly.
Overnight target range supports safe tight control above hypoglycemic thresholds.
Daytime target range keeps average glucose near 117 mg/dL.
Pre-bedtime target provides safe transition into overnight sleep hours.
5.5-hour duration of insulin action accurately mirrors observed tail-end meal recovery.
SMB and UAM activation effectively smooths postprandial rises without causing low glucose.
Specific activation boolean flags are null in export payload; confirm exact desired checkmarks in AAPS UI.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=45 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=30 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Delivery timing and max SMB basal minute caps are safely balanced with patient insulin sensitivity.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Safety boundaries allow necessary automated SMB delivery while preventing insulin stacking.
Autosens enable switches are null in profile export; verify activation state directly in AAPS app.
Minimum carb impact and max absorption duration support effective COB decay modeling.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain a 15-20 minute prebolus with full immediate meal boluses for standard carbohydrates, relying on active SMB/UAM automation to manage residual postprandial variability within the 5.5-hour DIA window.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Current meal timing strategies yield consistent return to baseline within 4 hours and 0% time below range.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log precise meal timestamps during high-fat/protein dinners to verify if e-carb modeling could further flatten evening postprandial curves.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 20-minute prebolus with 70% immediate bolus split.
exceptions.rationale: Keeps postprandial peak below 170 mg/dL with smooth recovery by 240 minutes.

exceptions.suggestion: Use 10-minute prebolus, 60% immediate bolus, and 20 g e-carbs over 120 minutes with 15-minute start offset.
exceptions.rationale: Allows UAM and SMB to safely distribute insulin for delayed absorption, bringing glucose from 188 mg/dL back to 115 mg/dL by 4 hours.

implementation_steps: Review analysis findings and confirm that 99.7% Time in Range aligns with personal clinical goals.
Open the AAPS mobile app preferences and verify SMB activation checkboxes (e.g., SMB with COB, SMB always) and Autosens switches.
Maintain current basal rates, carb ratios, ISF segments, and safety limits without making parameter changes.
Continue utilizing declared prebolus times (20 min for fast-carb breakfasts, 10 min for mixed brunches).
education: Time in Range above 70% with Time Below Range under 4% represents standard international consensus goals for diabetes management; achieving 99.7% TIR reflects exemplary parameter tuning.
Extended carbohydrates (e-carbs) in AAPS help model delayed fat and protein absorption, prompting UAM to deliver incremental SMBs rather than relying on a single large initial bolus.
safety_notes: This analysis is decision-support content only and does not constitute medical advice or prescriptions.
Always verify any proposed setting adjustments independently and consult your healthcare team before making changes to automated insulin delivery systems.
Only make profile adjustments one at a time, monitor continuous glucose readings closely, and ensure treatment for hypoglycemia is readily available.
